model_interpretation.claim: The baseline assigns one output to each thread in a 32x32 CTA, with neighboring lanes advancing across rows and therefore accessing row-major A and C with strides. This candidate keeps the same 32x32 output footprint but maps lanes across columns and assigns four rows at one column to each thread. That reuses each loaded B value across four independent FP32 accumulators and may improve coalescing while reducing CTA threads from 1024 to 256; the additional per-thread state may affect occupancy. The baseline is the measured one-output-per-thread control; candidate performance remains unmeasured.

items.subject: Multi-accumulator register-blocked SIMT microtiles
items.objective: Focus on register-blocked SIMT where each thread maintains multiple independent FP32 output accumulators, testing distinct row/column microtile mappings to reuse operands and improve arithmetic intensity. Compare against a one-output-per-thread control so the result is not merely a CTA tile-size comparison with T1; measure register/occupancy tradeoffs and correctness as well as repeated timing. Support tails and all valid dimensions and values, apply alpha/beta once per output, and preserve the entry point, buffers, stream, and full-FP32 requirement. Do not use tensor-core/reduced-precision math, extra allocations, or external math libraries.
